unit.sep: Derive ratio relationships and test angle-reference and measurement models.
unit.careers: Illustrative mathematical measurement/design modelling;no professional survey or unsafe field-operation qualification.
unit.focus: Acute trigonometric ratios,tables/calculators,complements,ratio relationships,special angles,elevation/depression and an observed-or-pending clinometer project.
unit.content: Trigonometric ratios of acute angles; Sines and Cosines of complementary angles; Trigonometric ratios of special angle; Application of trigonometric ratios
unit.phenomenon: A fictional height report uses a raw clinometer reading as the elevation and calls a finite device display the exact tangent of90°.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Named-angle side roles,rounded tables,exact triangle constructions,coordinate endpoint,parallel horizontals and calibrated instrument references.
unit.drivingQuestion: What is trigonometry? How do we use trigonometry in real-life situations?
unit.coreCompetencies:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner makes a simple clinometer using locally available material and uses it as a learning resource
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner discusses and makes observations about the sine and cosine of complementary angles, and applies trigonometric ratios in the solution of triangles
Digital literacy: the learner uses digital devices and other resources such as books, manuals, and journals to learn more about trigonometric ratios
unit.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes care of mathematical tables and calculators used in determining trigonometric ratios
Unity: the learner works in a group, for instance, when using an isosceles right-angled triangle and an equilateral triangle to generate the trigonometric ratios of special angles 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°
unit.pcis:
Environmental Education and Protection: the learner identifies shapes in the immediate environment that have right-angled triangles, and makes a simple clinometer using materials from the immediate environment
Parental Engagement and Empowerment: the learner gets support from parents/guardians to get resources to make a clinometer.

sections.title: 1. Ratios,table,calculator and complements
sections.prompt: For the CTG15right triangle,identify opposite,adjacent and hypotenuse relative toAandstate its three exact ratios. Read sin40°andcos50°from the supplied table and explain their complementary-angle relation. When an approved calculator is supplied,actually obtain tan30°in degree mode,record the real entry/full display and round to4decimal places;teacher separately records observation. Otherwise mark NOT OBSERVED andleaveactualcalculatorperformancepending.
sections.exemplar: OppositeBC5,adjacentAC12,hypotenuseAB13;sinA=5/13,cosA=12/13,tanA=5/12. sin40°=cos50°exactly by complementary side roles;both supplied rounded entries≈0.6428. Actual degree-mode tan30°≈0.5773502692→0.5774;accept actual model-specific entry/display with observation,not a fabricated record. Paper/table correctness does not certify device use.

sections.title: 2. Relate ratios and derive special-angle values
sections.prompt: Use your exact section1fractions to show tanA=sinA/cosA. With labelled drawings of the two supplied special-angle models,derive45°and30°/60°ratios and complete a four-row exact sin/cos/tan table for30°,45°,60°,90°. Explain separately why90°requires a limiting/coordinate endpoint and why its tangent is not a finite real value.
sections.exemplar: (5/13)/(12/13)=5/12. Unit-leg isosceles right triangle has hypotenuse√2;equilateral side2splits to legs1,√3,hypotenuse2. Exact rows(sin,cos,tan):30°(1/2,√3/2,1/√3);45°(1/√2,1/√2,1);60°(√3/2,1/2,√3);90°(1,0,notdefined). The first three come from nondegenerate right triangles;at90°the acute model collapses andthe coordinate/limit case gives sin/cos,whiletanwoulddivideby0.

sections.title: 3. Apply elevation and depression
sections.prompt: Draw and solve both CTG15paper cases with explicit horizontal references and units. Find the elevation target’s total height to2decimal places,including its sight-point height. Separately find the depression case’s horizontal distance;explain why its stated8mheight needs no extra body-height addition. State the level/straight-line model assumptions.
sections.exemplar: Elevation rise10tan30°=10/√3m,total1.4+10/√3≈7.17m. Separate depression distance8/tan45°=8m;the given8malready measures sight point above target level. Parallel horizontals support equal acute angles;horizontal baseline and level/reference assumptions are explicit. These are paper data,not actual measurements.
